cues.pt: Então você se posiciona, passa o peso pra frente, mão em cima — não

cues.en: to hold it. There's one more detail.

cues.ru: Вам нужно напрягать пресс, напрягать тело.

cues.es: Tienes que apretar el abdomen, tensar el cuerpo.

cues.ja: 腹筋に力を入れて、体を固める。
cues.ko: 복근에 힘주고 몸에 힘을 줘야 해요.
cues.zh: 要收紧腹肌，绷紧身体。

cues.ru: И стараться свести к минимуму любое движение.

cues.ru: Убираем, просто замираем и всё — ждём чуда.

cues.ja: 全部なくして、ピタッと止まって、奇跡を待つ。

cues.de: Jetzt von der Seite.
cues.ja: 横から見せます。

cues.es: Pasas el peso.

cues.fr: On transfère le poids.
cues.de: Gewicht verlagern.
cues.ja: 体重を移す。

cues.ru: Нога прижата.

cues.ru: Вес переносим.
cues.en: Shift the weight.
cues.es: Pasas el peso.
cues.pt: Passa o peso.
cues.fr: On transfère le poids.
cues.de: Gewicht verlagern.
cues.ja: 体重を移す。

cues.ru: Рука тоже напрягается — примерно так же, как когда просто стоите на руках.

cues.ja: 腕にも力が入る。普通の逆立ちと同じくらい。

en.en: Where do we start?
A training tip. You asked for more of these.
When you start, pay attention to the two surfaces that touch. Use bare skin on one side and fabric on the other.
Try a bare knee with fabric over the elbow.
Or switch it around. Cover the knee with cotton pants and leave the elbow bare.
That prevents slipping.
If your knee slides off your elbow, the freeze is much harder to practice.
Another trick is to put on an elbow pad.
Or roll it up like this, so it forms a little ridge.
That ridge makes this freeze easier to practice.
You'll feel a lot more stable as you lift up.
Or wear a knee pad and leave the elbow bare.
That works too. Start with those options.
Now, a common mistake when people start is how they place their hands.
They put this hand here, the other here, and end up in this position.
My weight is on my left hand. The other hand should line up with it.
I'll face you.
Here, my body forms one line.
My hand goes right here.
It shouldn't go over here.
Practice in this position and you'll learn the wrong weight shift.
Or you'll never learn it at all.
In this freeze, shift your weight along one line.
Notice how I stay in a straight line.
My legs and torso stay in line. My free arm hangs loose for balance.
Important.
Here's another view.
My right leg presses against the left to keep both legs in one line.
Shift your weight from here to here.
Bend your body slightly as you move into position.
Like this.
You don't have to hold your shoulder there or rotate it.
To make it easier, turn and reach your arm up.
Watch the knee here. This part is important.
Bend the knee deeply and you'll see a hollow.
That's where the point of your elbow goes.
With a shallow bend, the kneecap sticks out instead.
Bend it as far as you can to make that hollow.
What does that tell us?
A lot of beginners try the freeze without bending the leg all the way.
With the left knee open, they can't hold the position.
They think it's their balance or their strength.
What you need is a tighter bend, so the hollow behind your knee fits against the point of your elbow.
Bend as far as you can and set the knee on the elbow.
Once you're stable, lift off and hold.
As soon as you straighten the knee, you lose the hold and fall.
How do you practice this freeze with support?
Stack some books and put your free hand on them.
Getting into that line right away may be difficult.
Start with an easier version.
I found a chair instead of books.
So dusty.
Keep one line. Get into position and bend the knee deeply.
Move the chair well out, then shift your weight.
Use the chair for balance. Let that hand rest lightly on it.
Your left hand carries your weight. The chair only steadies you.
With books, build a stack at a height that works for you. Practice with that for support.
Now for the main part. How do you balance and hold the freeze longer?
Get your body into one line.
Keep your free arm up over your head.
Press your right leg against the left.
First, from the front.
Set up, then shift your weight forward.
Reach that arm up. Keep it over your head, right here.
Hold it there. One more detail.
Brace your abs and tense your body.
Keep movement to a minimum. No swaying or jerking.
Stay completely still and hold.
Now from the side.
Shift your weight.
Press your legs together.
Arm up top.
Keep still.
And hold.
Now the same thing from the back.
Shift your weight.
Legs together, in one line.
Arm on top. Hold it there.
Your arm is tense too, like in a regular handstand.
